question: Does a stronger multilingual embedding close the cross-lingual retrieval gap the live path shows?

query_set.note: one LLM-generated failure description per lesson, the same set the published L1-267 run used

corpus.source: data/lessons.json `url` -> lessons/**/*.md, title + body, first 6000 chars
corpus.note: the 8 lessons longer than the model's 2048-token input were auto-truncated by the API

model.name: gemini-embedding-001
model.note: embeddings only; no generative model was used or charged

also_measured.name: bge-m3
also_measured.note: the embedding production already indexes and serves; measured 2026-10-27 via the REST API, so the comparison is new-model vs current-model, not new-model vs the delivered system

limitations: the queries were generated from the target lesson, so absolute rates flatter any retriever; the arm-to-arm and arm-to-live deltas are the deliverable, not the level
pure cosine top-5 is not the production path: production is BM25 first with a semantic fallback only on an empty result
`no_match` means different things in the two arms (here: target not in top-5; live: the endpoint returned nothing) and must not be compared across them
the published L1-267 arms ran on an eval-worker corpus that was not refreshed before that run, so the comparison to them is directional
one query target (`proxy-corporativo-curl-timeout`) has no corpus row and is scored from target_url; it can only be a miss
the bge-m3 and gemini arms saw slightly different lesson text (bge-m3 got the same 6000-char truncation as the corpus; 8 gemini inputs hit its 2048-token cap), which can only understate bge-m3
